subject: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist — integration follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist (post-discovery)

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so your team has a single place to reference: 

Scope we discussed:
- Integration surface: Redwood SDK for server-side requests (Java/Python) + optional client-side embedders for offline embedding jobs.
- Auth: short-lived API keys + optional mTLS for private endpoints (you indicated compliance leans toward mTLS).
- Routing: per-route model pinning (low-latency model for chat, separate heavier model for embeddings/rerank).
- Structured output/tool calling: we support function-calling patterns and JSON-schema enforcement for predictable responses.
- Embeddings/rerankers: recommend separate embedding model endpoint and an in-line reranker for retrieval results.

Networking asks we need to move forward:
1) Will you want traffic to go over AWS VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) to Redwood?
2) Do you require IP allowlisting on our side, or only inbound allowlist from your egress?
3) Egress/NAT: what do your outbound IPs look like (CIDR or NAT ranges)?
4) DNS & mTLS: do you manage internal DNS for the VPC endpoints, and will you supply client certs for mTLS?

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll send the networking checklist (attached) and our VPC endpoints guide.
- Technical sync with our solutions engineer Jonas Weber and Marissa from Customer Success — can we target next week?
- Once we confirm CIDRs and mTLS approach, we can provide sample client configs and a test endpoint.

If you can reply with the answers to the four networking asks above and attach your network diagram, we’ll prepare the mutual action plan and draft a minimal firewall/IP rule set to share with your infra team.

Thanks,
Lauren

Hey Lauren —

Thanks for the summary — helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Yes, we prefer PrivateLink (AWS VPC endpoints) so traffic stays within AWS networking.
2) We will require IP allowlisting on any public egress; for private endpoints we expect mTLS + allowlisting on both sides if possible.
3) Egress/NAT: we have a set of NAT gateway IPs that we can share (see attached network diagram).
4) DNS: we manage internal Route53 private hosted zones. We can accept a TLS certificate bundle for mTLS; our security team will coordinate certificate exchange out-of-band (cc: devops@finpay.com).

Attaching: finpay-network-diagram.pdf

Can you also share an example client config (curl + Python snippet) and the minimum firewall rules you recommend?

Subject: RE: Follow-up: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist (technical details)

Hi Amit / Lauren —

Following up with more technical detail from our infra/solutions perspective. Notes below to prepare your infra team for the technical sync: 

Auth & SDKs
- We support API key auth over TLS for hosted endpoints; for PrivateLink endpoints we can enable mTLS and enforce client certs.
- SDKs (Python/Java/Go) support short-lived tokens and automatic rotation via our token endpoint.

Routing & models
- You can route by path or header; we recommend a separate endpoint for embeddings so you can scale those independently.
- Reranker can be invoked as a second-stage call (we provide batch endpoints for reranking top-K).

Network configuration checklist (high level)
- VPC Endpoint: AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) — provide us with the ENI subnets to validate routing.
- DNS: Private hosted zone delegation — we will provide endpoint hostnames to add to Route53.
- IP allowlist: provide NAT egress IPs — we will create a limited egress allowlist for callbacks and webhooks.
- mTLS: we will require a client cert for the initial handshake to the private endpoint; cert exchange can be done via SFTP or a signed URL.

Minimal firewall rules we typically ask for:
- outbound TCP 443 to the Redwood endpoint hostnames (or VPC endpoint ENIs)
- allow responses on ephemeral ports as configured by AWS

I'm attaching our Redwood VPC endpoints guide which includes example client configs (curl, Python) and sample IAM policy snippets. Jonas — can you join the sync to run through certificate exchange details and DNS delegation?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-vpc-endpoints-guide.pdf
